title: Partial and full liquid volumes of tanks with formed heads (closed forms of D. Jones, 'Calculating Tank Volume')

provenance.formulas: Jones D., Calculating Tank Volume (2015) [S1], as implemented and cited by fluids 1.3.1 fluids/geometry.py (MIT) [S2]
provenance.values: expected values copied from fluids 1.3.1 tests/test_geometry.py (sha256 3d154846de058dbcc5d8b88e3a4bd7598b5dd019830bc702c9b2430b045ff83b); the test comments say the h=24/60 (vertical) and h=36/84 (horizontal) rows are the worked examples of [S1]
provenance.independentCheck: re-implemented from the printed formulas in data/derive_expected.py (no fluids import): every value below is reproduced to <= 1e-12 relative; the horizontal conical case is checked by numerical integration of circular-segment areas (agrees to 1e-9 relative)
provenance.units: inputs in inches, volumes in US gallons (1 US gal = 231 in^3 exactly); llull tests convert to SI and compare in m^3

conventions.a: head depth (inside) beyond the tangent line; 2:1 ellipsoidal head a = D/4
conventions.f, k: torispherical dish radius = f*D, knuckle radius = k*D
conventions.h: liquid level measured from the lowest point of the vessel (vertical: head apex; horizontal: shell bottom)
conventions.vertical: bottom head only (no top head), as in [S1]
